title: feat: enable backup support for Git-based Docker Compose databases
summary:
When deploying a Docker Compose file via GitHub App (dockercompose buildpack), database services were not detected and no `ServiceDatabase` records were created, making backups unavailable. The root cause: `parseDockerComposeFile()` already called `isDatabaseImage()` in the Application path but never persisted the result as `ServiceDatabase` records (unlike the Service model path).

This PR adds a nullable `application_id` foreign key to `service_databases` (making `service_id` nullable), allowing `ServiceDatabase` records to be owned by either a `Service` or an `Application`. The Application compose parsing path now creates/updates `ServiceDatabase` records for detected database images, and prunes orphaned records when a database service is removed from the compose file. A new Databases tab appears in the application configuration page (dockercompose build pack only, when databases are detected), with per-database backup management.

Deployment/backup conflicts are handled by checking for in-progress deployments at the start of the backup job and releasing the job for retry after 60 seconds. All existing paths that referenced `ServiceDatabase->service` have been guarded to fall back to `ServiceDatabase->application` when `application_id` is set.
testing: Vendor dependencies could not be installed in this environment (PHP 8.3 vs required 8.4). Added `tests/Feature/ApplicationComposeDatabaseBackupTest.php` covering: ServiceDatabase creation with application_id, team resolution via application relationship chain, and `isBackupSolutionAvailable()` for postgres/non-database images. Reviewed all service->server access paths in backup jobs, Livewire components, and helpers and guarded each one for the application-owned case.

## Changes

When deploying a Docker Compose file via GitHub App (dockercompose buildpack), database services were not persisted as `ServiceDatabase` records, making backups unavailable.

- Added nullable `application_id` FK to `service_databases` and made `service_id` nullable
- `ServiceDatabase` model now supports both Service and Application ownership via `application()` relationship
- `Application` model gains a `serviceDatabase()` `HasMany` relationship
- `parseDockerComposeFile()` Application path now creates/updates `ServiceDatabase` records for detected databases, and deletes orphaned records when the compose changes
- `DatabaseBackupJob` resolves server/network from `application->destination` when `application_id` is set, and aborts with a 60-second retry if a deployment is in progress
- `ScheduledDatabaseBackup::server()`, `BackupEdit`, `BackupExecutions`, `StartDatabaseProxy`, `CleanupStuckedResources`, and the backup download route all handle the application-owned case
- New Databases tab in the application configuration page (dockercompose only, when databases exist) with per-database backup management via the existing `ScheduledBackups` and `BackupEdit` components
